sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: 106 Exploring Society: India and Beyond Our Cultural Heritage and Knowledge Traditions Indian culture, by any estimate, is several millenniums old.
sections.source_evidence: 106 Exploring Society: India and Beyond Our Cultural Heritage and Knowledge Traditions Indian culture, by any estimate, is several millenniums old.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: Like any ancient tree, it has many roots and many branches.
sections.source_evidence: Like any ancient tree, it has many roots and many branches.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: And from the trunk emerge many branches, which are different manifestations of Indian culture, yet united by a common trunk.
sections.source_evidence: And from the trunk emerge many branches, which are different manifestations of Indian culture, yet united by a common trunk.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: Some of these branches are about art, literature, science, medicine, religion, the art of governance, martial arts, and so on.
sections.source_evidence: Some of these branches are about art, literature, science, medicine, religion, the art of governance, martial arts, and so on.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: There are also ‘schools of thought’, by which we mean groups of thinkers or spiritual seekers who share similar ideas about human life, the world, etc.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: Many archaeologists and scholars have pointed out that some of India’s cultural roots go all the way to the Indus or Harappan or Sindhu-Sarasvatī civilisation (which we visit in Chapter 6).

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: Later on, over time, hundreds of schools of thought emerged in India.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: We will see here a few early schools, which have shaped India into a country with a unique personality.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: By understanding them and their roots, we can understand ‘India, that is Bharat’ better.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: The word “Veda” comes from the Sanskrit vid which means ‘knowledge’ (hence vidyā, for instance).

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: In fact, there are four Vedas — the Ṛig Veda, the Yajur Veda, the Sāma Veda and the Atharva Veda.

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: They are the most ancient texts of India, and indeed among the most ancient in the world.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: The Vedas consist of thousands of hymns — prayers in the form of poems and songs — that were recited orally, not written.

sections.content: Those hymns were composed in the Sapta Sindhava region (which we visit in Chapter 5).
